paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the average change percentage by initial accuracy for a language model, specifically Claude on the MMLU-Pro benchmark. The x-axis, labeled “Turn Number,” ranges from 1 to 7 with tick labels spaced at intervals of one, and represents the number of successive turns in a conversation. The y-axis, labeled “Change Percentage (%)”, uses a linear scale and extends from approximately 10% to 50%, with tick labels spaced at increments of 10%. The orange line represents the initial correct answer, and begins at a value of approximately 10% at turn number 1, steadily increasing to approximately 45% at turn number 6. The maroon line represents the initial incorrect answer, which starts at approximately 5% at turn number 1, and remains relatively flat at approximately 10% throughout the seven turns.
